releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- aacd45a: Expose the provenance of verification and review evidence in `guard_status`.

    - `guard_status.lastVerify` now reports its observation timestamp and duration beside the command, pass state, freshness, evidence id, and commit hash. A configured `verifyCommand` that runs green therefore leaves a record naming when it ran and the commit it covered, instead of only an anonymous evidence id.
    - `guard_status.lastReview` now reports its observation timestamp together with `recorderSessionID`, `recorderRole` (`root` or `subagent`), and `targetSessionID`. Under `requireSubagentReview`, this shows that an approval came from a subagent session rather than the root session it was recorded for.
    - `record_review` keeps the recorder lineage on the stored verdict, and the durable review cache carries the same optional fields. `record_review` itself stays registered for every session; a deny-all reviewer toolset still needs the host permission grant in its own agent definition.

### Patch Changes

- 7ef8009: Allow sanctioned scratch writes, reclaim leaked file claims by TTL, and name the verify-config source.

    - `/tmp/opencode` is now a write allowance rather than a block with a nicer message. A write is allowed for a real session and only while the target's canonical location stays inside that exact directory. The root must be a real directory. A symlink that leaves it, a sibling that shares the prefix, a `..` traversal out of it, and a session-less write stay blocked. The todo and feature-branch gates still apply, as they do to every mutation. A scratch write skips the file-claim, prior-read, and mutation-evidence steps because it is not repository state.
    - A leaked file claim is now reclaimed by two audited rules, both scoped to the contended paths so a long-running command elsewhere keeps its claim. The existing idle rule stays. A new TTL rule releases a claim older than `claimTtlMs` (default five minutes, `WORKFLOW_GUARD_CLAIM_TTL_MS` wins) even when the owner record cannot be read, which covers a deleted session and a server restart. The reclaim is journaled as `claim_ttl_expired` with the owner and claim age, and the conflict message names the owner, age, and reclaim step.
    - `guard_status` reports `projectConfig.configPath`, the project config file actually read, plus `verifyCommandSource` (`environment`, `project-config`, `auto-detected`, or null). A null `verifyCommand` with a null source means the repository has neither a configured nor a detectable command, which is now distinguishable from an auto-detected command.
    - A reviewer agent's access to `record_review` is a host permission grant, not a guard policy. The tool stays registered for every session regardless of `requireReview`, so an agent with a deny-all permission list must allow it in its own definition. This release documents that lever and covers the registration with a regression test.

### Patch Changes

- 553810f: Narrow the V2 event subscription, honor the per-call abort signal, and wake the title settle on the delivered rename.

    - `ctx.event.subscribe()` now passes its `types` filter, so only the ten event types `handleV2Event` acts on cross the stream. Every other host event is dropped by the server before it reaches the plugin. The list is exported as `V2_EVENT_TYPES`, and the suite asserts it matches the handler's comparisons in both directions and that every entry is in `EventManifest.ServerDefinitions`. A type added to the handler but not the filter would otherwise become dead code that still compiles, which is how the previously repaired handlers broke.
    - The long-running guard tools that spawn subprocesses (`guard_worktree_create`, `guard_worktree_cleanup`, `guard_review_rubric`, `guard_recovery_restore`) now stop before starting work when the session was already interrupted. They read the per-call abort signal, which OpenCode 2's promise-layer tool context names `signal` and OpenCode 1's names `abort`. A cancelled call returns a `Cancelled` result instead of running to its own timeout. The check is placed before the work because `spawnSync` cannot observe an abort mid-flight. Short git-backed reads keep their five-second bound and are out of scope.
    - The title settle wait now ends as soon as the delivered `session.renamed` event reports that the title committed, instead of always sleeping the full 8 x 250 ms poll. The wake-up is registered before the session read, so a rename that lands during the read is still observed rather than costing an extra interval. A host that does not emit the event keeps the exact previous timing, and `titleSettleWorkaround: false` still disables the wait entirely.
    - `test:install` no longer fails its own cleanup with `ENOTEMPTY`. `opencode debug config` auto-starts a detached `serve --service` under the probe's isolated `XDG_*` roots, and killing the probe child left that service running and writing into the temporary project. The harness now stops every service it started before removing the directory, then retries the removal.

### Patch Changes

- 7db69f8: Restore V2 enforcement that keyed on event types the host never delivers, and honor the user interrupt.

    The V2 event stream is served from `EventManifest.ServerDefinitions`. A type present in `Definitions` but absent from that manifest is never delivered, even when a plugin handles it. Three handlers were built on such types.

    - Tool-outcome telemetry now records from `ctx.tool.hook("execute.after")` instead of the never-delivered `session.message.content.updated` type. The repeated-failure circuit breaker and the Policy 25 live-documentation research floor were dead on V2, because `getFailureCount()` could only return 0. A failed tool call now accrues failure debt and a successful call clears it, preserving the existing failure signature (`sha256(tool \0 error)`).
    - `session.execution.interrupted` is handled, so a user interrupt (Esc) suspends automatic continuation on V2. Only reason `user` suspends. `shutdown`, `superseded`, and `inactivity` are host-lifecycle events and leave continuation state alone. Ralph runs record the `user_stopped` outcome in the same handler, so both continuation budgets agree.
    - The MCP inventory refresh now triggers on the delivered `mcp.status.changed` instead of the never-delivered `mcp.tools.changed`, so a guarded server connecting mid-session is guarded without waiting for the next session. Widening stays additive; static tokens are never removed.
    - The idle handler now handles both delivered idle types: `session.status` with `status.type === "idle"` and the deprecated `session.idle`. Which one the server publishes is not settled, so relying on a single one could silently disable automatic continuation. A host that emits both for one transition still sends a single prompt, because the send holds a per-session in-flight lock. Side effects are unchanged.
    - The `command.executed` audit handler was removed. It never ran on V2, and no delivered event carries a slash-command invocation, so Policy 13 now documents that audit as V1-only.
    - Automatic continuation passes `delivery: "queue"` and `resume: true` explicitly instead of relying on host defaults.
    - The V2 entrypoint no longer imports the V1 entrypoint. `guardToolCall`, `guardToolDecision`, and `buildCompactionContext` moved to `src/lib/guard-api.ts`, which breaks an import cycle that pulled the V1 file and its SDK subtree into a V2 host. The builtin tool-description suffixes moved to `src/lib/tool-descriptions.ts` so both hosts share one copy.
    - Block toasts are no longer awaited on V2, where the client shim supplies no TUI surface. The thrown tool error still carries the block reason to the model.

### Patch Changes

- c2d4fad: Judge git commands against the tree they actually run in, and stop denying cwd-dependent commands from the wrong checkout.

    - `parseGitInvocation` accepts the shell's `workdir` as its base directory, so branch, mergeability, and protected-branch checks judge the checkout the command runs in rather than the session-bound one.
    - A linked worktree of the same repository is no longer treated as foreign state for git mutations and pushes.
    - PR preflight resolves `gh --head` / `-H` and `az --source-branch` to the worktree holding that branch, and the merge check takes the resolved ref instead of `HEAD`. A named source branch that no local checkout holds is refused, because review and merge evidence bind to the content of a checkout: substituting the caller's tree would let an approval of one tree satisfy a PR that publishes another.
    - The V2 permission seat defers cwd-dependent commands (`git push`, history writes, branch creation, PR creation) with code `repository_unidentified` instead of judging the session-bound checkout. An explicit `-C`/`--git-dir`/`--work-tree`/`GIT_DIR` stays decisive, and so does a push to `main` or `master`; a configured `protectedBranches` destination defers like any other cwd-dependent verdict. A block from another policy in the same compound command keeps its denial.
    - A repository claim is only an assignment: `GIT_DIR=` inside a commit message is message text, not a repository selector, including through `env`/`sudo`/`timeout` wrappers. A repository selection that cannot be resolved (`git -C $OTHER_REPO`) stays a boundary block even when the session's own workspace is a repository, because the linked-worktree exemption would otherwise resolve it to the workspace's own root.
    - A shell `workdir` in a different repository is not judged. The command runs there, so a relative target (`rm -rf dist`, `> artifact.txt`) would be validated against the workspace root while changing another tree. Recognized mutations and git writes in that workdir are blocked as a workspace escape, and reads there stay allowed. Recognized shell mutations are validated against the linked worktree the command actually runs in, so a `workdir` in a linked worktree of the same repository is judged where it lands.
    - An in-command `cd`, `pushd`, and `popd` now moves the directory later segments are judged in. `planShellSegments` walks the command and resolves each segment's own root, so `cd <other-repo> && git commit` is a write in that other repository instead of a commit in the session's checkout. The same walk drives shell-mutation validation, redirect snapshots, and the protected-branch check, so `cd nested && echo x > artifact.txt` is judged where the file actually lands. A `cd` inside a grouping subshell is scoped to it, and the subshell's directory stack goes with it. A `cd` inside a conditional or loop body is followed only as far as determinacy allows: that body runs in the current shell, but which body runs depends on a condition, so a construct whose body changes directory leaves the later directory undetermined and a mutation after it fails closed.
    - A newline separates commands exactly like `;`, so a newline-separated `cd` moves the tree of the lines that follow. The walk plans the raw command text instead of a whitespace-flattened copy, because flattening newlines erased that separator and a `cd <other-repo>` on its own line moved nothing.
    - A heredoc body belongs to the segment that introduces it, so its newlines no longer split it into separate commands. One header line may introduce several bodies (`cat <<A <<B`), and all of them stay with that segment. A body is scanned as code when the command reading it executes it (`bash`, `sh`, `python`, `source`, and the other launchers, or a pipe into a command), so a body feeding `cat` stays prose and documentation quoting a blocked command shape remains writable.
